_.name: English (en)
analytics.bouncesHint: Bounces over Sent. Hard = permanent failures, soft = temporary ones, complaints = spam reports; every bounce is counted, so a subscriber with a hard and a soft bounce appears in both.
analytics.clientsHint: Email clients are recorded from the release of this feature onward; older activity shows as Unknown. Apple Mail includes its privacy proxy, which pre-fetches images, so its views are inflated by machine opens. A click is the browser the link opened in, not the mail client. Percentages are each client's share of the column in this table.
analytics.clientsTierHint: The tiers group the rows above. They are shown separately and are never added together: the sum would be a "real opens" figure this data cannot support. "From client software" is a ceiling on human opens, not a count of them — mail-security gateways pre-fetch with spoofed browser User-Agents and land here. "Via a provider proxy" means a real mailbox exists but the open timing is unreliable; Apple Mail sits here conservatively, because its privacy proxy and a real open cannot be told apart by User-Agent. "Declared machines" is non-interactive software (a link preview does mean a person shared the link). "No tier claimed" covers Other, the unnamed bare-Mozilla bucket and Unknown. On the Clicks column the tiers mean something weaker: a click's User-Agent is the browser the link opened in, so proxies barely appear and a browser click is usually a person — except that link-prefetching gateways also click, which is why "From client software" stays a ceiling on both columns.
analytics.clicksHint: Subscribers who clicked at least one link, counted once each (unique clicks), over Sent.
analytics.conversions.hint: Sales, with the order count underneath. Both are attributed orders read side by side — never incremental lift. — means the campaign is not covered by that measure (a missing campaign is not zero); orders are counted by purchase time within the date range.
analytics.conversions.matchedHelp: Matched: Tracked orders, plus paid orders placed by a recipient within 5 days (120 h) after clicking this campaign, matched by email; a Tracked order stays with its Tracked campaign, any other order goes to the most recent qualifying click. Brand-only sales. Attributed, not incremental. From {floor}.
analytics.conversions.arrivals: Matched orders by day after send
analytics.conversions.undated: {n} more Matched from evergreen campaigns (no single send day).
analytics.conversions.noOrders: No orders for these campaigns in this date range.
analytics.conversions.stale: Tracked is from an earlier snapshot.
analytics.conversions.title: Conversions
analytics.matrix.viewsHelp: Distinct subscribers who viewed the campaign (the one Views definition).
analytics.matrix.clicksHelp: Distinct subscribers who clicked (each person once).
analytics.matrix.creator: Creator
analytics.matrix.shopLinksHelp: Shop-link clicks by the clicker's shop-link kind (the one held at send, else the one held now), counted like Clicks. — means the campaign has no shop link.
analytics.matrix.fblHelp: Complaints received through the providers' feedback loops.
analytics.matrix.gpHelp: Google Postmaster's spam rate for the campaign's brand on its send day, coloured against the thresholds stored with it.
analytics.matrix.gpNone: Google reported no spam rate for {brand} on {date}.
analytics.matrix.gpNoBrand: No single brand, so no Postmaster domain.
analytics.matrix.note: Campaigns with activity in the 60 Mountain days ending yesterday ({from} to {to}). A broadcast is listed when it started in that window, with everything recorded for it through yesterday; a journey is listed when it sent in the window, with its sends and activity in the window only (each person counted once, on their first view or click). %/$ shows every count over the row's Sent and conversions as sales; # shows counts and orders. Views are inflated by auto-opens (Apple MPP). Shop link attribution counts shop-link clickers by their shop-link kind (— = no shop link in the campaign).
analytics.conversions.trackedHelp: Tracked: orders David's UTM attribution credits to this campaign (last captured email click, no window), with sales counted for this campaign's brand only. Attributed, not incremental. From {floor}.
analytics.dateRangeHint: From and To limit which views, clicks and bounces are counted for the selected campaigns — they don't filter the campaign list.
analytics.linksHint: Clickers per link: a subscriber who clicked two links counts once in each, so this total can exceed Clicks, which counts each subscriber once.
analytics.rateHint: Views, clicks and bounces within the date range are shown as a rate over the selected campaigns' Sent (each campaign over its own Sent in the ring), with the count in parentheses.
analytics.locationHint: Location is recorded as of 29 Sept. 2026; older activity shows as Unknown. Views are located by the mail client's image proxy (Gmail, Apple Mail), so view countries skew toward the proxy's location, while clicks come from the reader's device. A subscriber seen in two countries counts once in each, so the columns need not add up to the totals above. Percentages are each country's share of the views or clicks in this table, not a rate over Sent.
analytics.nonIndividualTracking: The counts are non-unique as individual subscriber tracking is turned off.
analytics.shopLinksHint: Clicks on the campaign's shop links, by the kind of shop link each recipient held when the campaign was sent (recorded at send for broadcasts since frozen attribution was released; campaign 215's was reconstructed; automations and older sends use the kind held today). Rate = those clicks over the recipients who held that kind at send. No link = no stored shop link for that brand, so the click went to the brand site.
analytics.shopLinksNoSnapshot: No audience snapshot for this selection
analytics.shopLinksPartial: Rate covers only the selected campaigns that have an audience snapshot.
analytics.trackingDisabled: E-mail tracking is globally disabled. No new views or clicks are being recorded.

brands.tips.alarmComplaints: CloudWatch alarm on this brand's SES complaint rate: OK, ALARM, or INSUFFICIENT_DATA (no recent sends). Alarm states never change the SES status.

brands.tips.verdict: Gmail's deliverability verdict. NEEDS_WORK = Issues; COMPLIANT with USER_FEEDBACK_LOW = Needs attention; MESSAGE_VOLUME_LOW = Insuf data.

users.sessionExpiredStashed:
Your session timed out, but your unsaved edits have been kept in this browser. After you sign in again you will be asked whether to restore them.

They cannot be restored if:

  • more than 7 days pass before you sign in again
  • a different user signs in on this browser
  • the campaign has been started or sent in the meantime

If someone else saves this campaign before you return, you will be warned before your edits replace theirs.

campaigns.evergreenHelp: An automation runs until you cancel it. Pause to edit; subscribers who join while paused receive the updated email on resume.
campaigns.evergreenDelayHelp: 0 sends on join. A higher number is a delayed follow-up, for example a tip sheet 7 days after a first purchase. On a No-purchase series or Post-purchase series step list it is always 0: the list's own days setting decides the timing.
campaigns.evergreenTriggerLocked: This list fills automatically from purchases or a No-purchase series / Post-purchase series step, so its campaign is always an Automation.
campaigns.reengageQueueNote: This is a re-engagement queue list. Either way of sending counts as the sunset ask: an Automation (0 days after joining) asks each person on their own timeline as they arrive — recommended for new brands; a broadcast sends the ask in batches when you want control over timing and volume, for example to catch up a large imported queue.
campaigns.evergreenOneList: An automation must target exactly one list.
campaigns.evergreenNoSchedule: An automation cannot be scheduled. It starts sending when you start it.
campaigns.evergreenNotOptin: An opt-in campaign cannot be an automation.
campaigns.evergreenCollision: Another automation ({name}) is already running on this list with the same delay. Cancel it first.
campaigns.evergreenPauseToEdit: This automation is running. Pause it to edit.
campaigns.evergreenNoPurchaseDelay: An automation on a No-purchase series or Post-purchase series step list must send on join (0 days after joining). The list's own days setting already decides when members come due.
campaigns.noPurchaseListNotice: This is a No-purchase series or Post-purchase series step list: the daily sweep fills it with the members who come due. Start this automation before the first member comes due, and never import into or hand-add subscribers to this list.
campaigns.broadcastToTriggerWarning: {lists} fills automatically from purchases or a No-purchase series / Post-purchase series step, so its members are partway through a journey. Sending a one-off email to it is usually a mistake.
campaigns.idScopeHelp: Showing only the campaigns of the last send (from a Brand Usage link). Close it, or change the list, brand or scope, to show every campaign.
campaigns.statusScopeHelp: Showing only campaigns with this status (from a Dashboard link). Close it, or change the list, brand or scope, to show every status.
campaigns.evergreenLocked: The automation setting and the target lists cannot be changed once a campaign has started. Cancel it and create a new one.

subscribers.backfillHelp: Leave on for imports of existing subscribers. Turn off only when the file contains genuinely new signups that should receive automations (welcome emails).

settings.general.langEnableHelp: Shows the Language field on campaigns. Turn on only once subscribers carry a language attribute — until then every campaign in a language other than English has no audience.

The recipients it could not reach are recorded in campaign_send_failures (campaign id, subscriber, error) — re-sending to them is a manual decision. dashboard.blocklistedHelp: Blocklisted subscribers on the public lists in scope
dashboard.chartsNote: Daily, Mountain time. Clicks through yesterday; Sends through the latest daily SES read (each morning). Live counts for a send: open the campaign.
dashboard.conversionsChart.title: Clicks and conversions
dashboard.conversionsChart.note: Daily, Mountain time, by purchase date. Matched: Tracked orders, plus paid orders within 5 days after an email click (the line). Tracked: UTM-attributed orders from the BI export (the shaded area, when shown) — the gap between them is orders our click data found that the UTM export did not. Recent days fill in as orders arrive. Attributed, not incremental.
dashboard.clientsWindow: The 31 days up to the latest view (views) and the latest click (clicks). Counts here are events, not people — one person clicking three links is three — whereas the Overview above counts one clicker per subscriber per campaign.
dashboard.locationHint: Location is recorded as of 29 Sept. 2026; older activity shows as Unknown. Views are located by the mail client's image proxy (Gmail, Apple Mail), so view countries skew toward the proxy's location, while clicks come from the reader's device. Every view and click is counted, as the charts above; the Analytics Location table counts a subscriber once per campaign. Percentages are each country's share of the views or clicks in this table, not a rate over Sent.
dashboard.matrix.blockedHelp: Subscribers on this brand's public lists with status blocklisted
dashboard.matrix.blocksHelp: 5.7.x provider blocks — a subset of hBounces, no fixed target; the earliest reputation signal
dashboard.matrix.note: Sent, engagement and conversions cover the 60 Mountain days ending yesterday (SES daily sends, through the latest daily SES read); every engagement rate is over Sent. Conversions show sales under %/$ and orders under #. Views are inflated by auto-opens (Apple MPP) — compare across brands, don't read as absolute. Subscribers are the brand's public lists now. GP S% is Google Postmaster's spam rate, the worst day in the last 7, blank when Gmail reports insufficient data.
dashboard.matrix.sentHelp: SES sends over the 60 Mountain days ending yesterday -- the denominator of every engagement rate
dashboard.matrix.spamFlaggedHelp: Gmail's compliance verdict flags user-reported spam — see the brand page.
dashboard.matrix.spamHelp: Google Postmaster spam rate, the worst day in the last 7

dashboard.usage.noPurchaseHelp: The No-purchase series by day: Day 0 is the welcome automation on the brand's newsletter list, then the 2, 5 and 10-day steps (no purchase since joining). Each step scores 5 when active and 2 when idle.
series.welcomeDay0: Day 0 Welcome: Introduce the brand, explain its value proposition, and provide any promised signup incentive.
series.welcomeDay2: Day 2 Gentle conversion reminder: "Still exploring? Here's why customers love [Brand]." Highlight bestsellers and one or two convincing benefits.
series.welcomeDay5: Day 5 Address purchase hesitation: "A few reasons to feel good about your first order." Include authentic testimonials, product education, shipping or return assurances, and FAQs.
series.welcomeDay10: Day 10 Final conversion nudge: "Ready when you are." Reinforce value; consider an incentive only if justified by brand economics. Avoid artificial urgency.
series.postPurchaseDay0: Day 0 Thank you: Thank them for their first order and set delivery expectations. No sales pitch.
series.postPurchaseDay5: Day 5 Getting started: Around delivery: how to use the product, tips for best results, where to get help.
series.postPurchaseDay14: Day 14 How's it going?: About a week after delivery: ask for a review or feedback, and share what other customers love.
series.postPurchaseDay30: Day 30 Your next favorite: Complementary products or a refill reminder. Skipped if they've already ordered again.
series.welcomeLegacy: Legacy step: Outside the standard No-purchase series (2, 5, 10 days). It keeps sending but does not count toward the score.
series.postPurchaseLegacy: Legacy step: Outside the standard Post-purchase series (5, 14, 30 days). It keeps sending but does not count toward the score.
dashboard.usage.skippedHelp: Active subscribers in this language on a brand list whose campaigns in the last 60 days (Mountain time, ending yesterday) were all in other specific languages — finished broadcasts and running evergreens; a campaign with no language reaches everyone and covers every language. Each subscriber counts once. Subscribers with another or no language are not counted. 0 means none skipped — a campaign in this language ran, the brand's lists have no subscribers in this language, or there was no campaign activity in the window.

settings.performance.batchSizeHelp: The number of subscribers to pull from the database in a single iteration. Each iteration pulls subscribers from the database, sends messages to them, and then moves on to the next iteration to pull the next batch. This should ideally be higher than the maximum achievable throughput (concurrency * message_rate).
settings.performance.cacheSlowQueriesHel: Only enable this on large databases that have slowed down significantly. Caches list subscriber counts, dashboard statistics etc.
settings.performance.concurrencyHelp: Maximum concurrent worker (threads) that will attempt to send messages simultaneously.
settings.performance.maxErrThresholdHelp: The number of errors (eg: SMTP timeouts while e-mailing) a running campaign should tolerate before it is paused for manual investigation or intervention. Set to 0 to never pause.
settings.performance.messageRateHelp: Maximum number of messages to be sent out per second per worker in a second. If concurrency = 10 and message_rate = 10, then up to 10x10=100 messages may be pushed out every second. This, along with concurrency, should be tweaked to keep the net messages going out per second under the target message servers rate limits if any.
settings.performance.name: Performance
settings.performance.slidingWindowDurati: Duration of the sliding window period (m for minute, h for hour).
settings.performance.slidingWindowHelp: Limit the total number of messages that are sent out in given period. On reaching this limit, messages are be held from sending until the time window clears.
settings.performance.slidingWindowRateHe: Maximum number of messages to send within the window duration.
